en.title: Whether Tree Path Characters Can Be Rearranged into a Palindrome
en.description:
Each node of a tree carries a lowercase letter. Each query asks whether all characters on the unique path between two nodes (including both endpoints) can be rearranged into a palindrome.

This site has made the standard input and output explicit; any range not given by the source is marked as this site's protocol.
en.input: The first line contains n q, and the second line contains n lowercase letters; then n−1 undirected edges follow, then q pairs of query nodes, 0-indexed. 1≤n,q≤100000.
en.explanation: Example 1: the path aba can be rearranged, while ab has two characters with odd frequency, so output 1, 0. Example 2: the two a's in aa can be paired, so output 1. Example 3: all three characters in bac have odd counts, so output 0.
hints: Maintain the character-parity bitmask from the root to each node, and find the lowest common ancestor LCA with binary lifting. The path mask is mask[u] xor mask[v] xor letter-bit[LCA], and it works if at most one bit is set.
